source_text: Al mal tiempo, buena cara
english_translation: To bad weather, good face
Cultural_Context: Face difficulties with a positive attitude; maintain composure in tough times.

source_text: De tal palo, tal astilla
english_translation: From such a stick, such a chip
Cultural_Context: Children often resemble their parents in character/behavior (like father, like son).

source_text: Dime con quién andas, y te diré quién eres
english_translation: Tell me with whom you walk, and I’ll tell you who you are
Cultural_Context: You are judged by the company you keep.

source_text: Un clavo saca otro clavo
english_translation: One nail drives out another
Cultural_Context: To forget one love, find another (move on from heartbreak).

source_text: Ojos que no ven, corazón que no siente
english_translation: Eyes that don’t see, heart that doesn’t feel
Cultural_Context: What you don’t know doesn’t hurt you.

source_text: Más vale pájaro en mano que cien volando
english_translation: A bird in the hand is worth more than one hundred flying
Cultural_Context: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush (value what you have).

source_text: Al mejor escribano se le va un borrón
english_translation: To the best scribe a blot escapes
Cultural_Context: Even experts make mistakes (nobody's perfect).

source_text: No hay mal que por bien no venga
english_translation: No bad from which good does not come
Cultural_Context: Every cloud has a silver lining (good comes from bad).

source_text: El que mucho abarca, poco aprieta
english_translation: He who grasps much, holds little
Cultural_Context: Don't bite off more than you can chew (overambition fails).

source_text: A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda
english_translation: To he who rises early, God helps him
Cultural_Context: The early bird catches the worm (diligence rewarded).

source_text: Allí donde fueres, haz lo que vieres
english_translation: Wherever you go, do what you see
Cultural_Context: When in Rome, do as the Romans do (adapt to local customs).

source_text: No por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano
english_translation: Not by waking up early does dawn come sooner
Cultural_Context: You can't rush things (patience needed).

source_text: Cada loco con su tema
english_translation: Each madman with his theme
Cultural_Context: Everyone has their own quirks/obsessions.

source_text: El que la hace, la paga
english_translation: He who does it, pays for it
Cultural_Context: What goes around comes around (consequences).

source_text: En boca cerrada no entran moscas
english_translation: Flies don't enter a closed mouth
Cultural_Context: Keep quiet to avoid trouble.

source_text: Cría cuervos y te sacarán los ojos
english_translation: Raise crows and they'll peck out your eyes
Cultural_Context: Beware of ingratitude (those you help may betray you).

source_text: A río revuelto, ganancia de pescadores
english_translation: In troubled waters, fishermen profit
Cultural_Context: Chaos benefits opportunists.

source_text: No todo lo que brilla es oro
english_translation: Not all that glitters is gold
Cultural_Context: Appearances can deceive.

source_text: El hábito no hace al monje
english_translation: The habit does not make the monk
Cultural_Context: Don't judge a book by its cover.

source_text: Perro que ladra no muerde
english_translation: A barking dog doesn't bite
Cultural_Context: Those who talk big often don't act.

source_text: Camarón que se duerme, se lo lleva la corriente
english_translation: The shrimp that falls asleep is carried away by the current
Cultural_Context: Don't be complacent or you'll fall behind.

source_text: Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho
english_translation: From saying to doing there's a long way
Cultural_Context: Actions speak louder than words.

source_text: A mal tiempo, buena cara
english_translation: To bad weather, good face
Cultural_Context: Put on a brave face in difficulties.

source_text: La avaricia rompe el saco
english_translation: Greed breaks the sack
Cultural_Context: Too much greed leads to loss.

source_text: Quien siembra vientos, recoge tempestades
english_translation: He who sows winds reaps storms
Cultural_Context: You reap what you sow (negative actions return worse).

source_text: El que calla, otorga
english_translation: He who is silent grants
Cultural_Context: Silence implies consent.

source_text: El tiempo todo lo cura
english_translation: Time heals everything
Cultural_Context: Time mends wounds.

source_text: A palabras necias, oídos sordos
english_translation: To foolish words, deaf ears
Cultural_Context: Ignore nonsense.

source_text: No hay peor ciego que el que no quiere ver
english_translation: There is no worse blind person than the one who doesn't want to see
Cultural_Context: Willful ignorance is the worst.

source_text: El que espera, desespera
english_translation: He who waits, despairs
Cultural_Context: Don't wait too long (act decisively).

source_text: El que mucho abarca poco aprieta
english_translation: He who embraces too much holds little tightly
Cultural_Context: Don't try to do too many things at once — you'll end up doing none well (overcommitment leads to failure).

source_text: A falta de pan, buenas son tortas
english_translation: In the absence of bread, cakes are good
Cultural_Context: When you can't have the best, settle for the next best thing (make do with what you have).

source_text: El que a buen árbol se arrima, buena sombra le cobija
english_translation: He who leans against a good tree gets good shade
Cultural_Context: Associate with good people and you'll benefit from their influence/protection.

source_text: De tal palo tal astilla
english_translation: From such a tree such a splinter
Cultural_Context: Children inherit the traits/behavior of their parents.

source_text: Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres
english_translation: Tell me who you hang out with and I'll tell you who you are
Cultural_Context: Your character is revealed by the company you keep.

source_text: Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando
english_translation: A bird in the hand is worth more than one hundred flying
Cultural_Context: It's better to keep what you already have than risk losing it for something uncertain.

source_text: A quien madruga Dios le ayuda
english_translation: God helps the early riser
Cultural_Context: Hard work and early rising are rewarded with success and divine favor.

source_text: Allí donde fueres haz lo que vieres
english_translation: Wherever you go, do what you see
Cultural_Context: Adapt to local customs and behavior when in a new place or culture.

source_text: No hay mal que dure cien años ni cuerpo que lo resista
english_translation: No evil lasts a hundred years nor body that endures it
Cultural_Context: Even the worst situations eventually end; nothing is permanent.

source_text: El que no arriesga no gana
english_translation: He who does not risk does not win
Cultural_Context: You must take chances to achieve success or gain rewards.

source_text: En casa del herrero cuchillo de palo
english_translation: In the blacksmith's house, wooden knife
Cultural_Context: People often lack or neglect the very thing they are expert in providing to others.

source_text: El que se pica ajos come
english_translation: He who gets annoyed eats garlic
Cultural_Context: If someone reacts defensively to a comment, it probably applies to them.

source_text: A mal tiempo buena cara
english_translation: To bad weather a good face
Cultural_Context: Maintain dignity and positivity during hardship or misfortune.

source_text: La ocasión la pintan calva
english_translation: Opportunity is bald
Cultural_Context: You must seize opportunities quickly because they don't last long.

source_text: El muerto al hoyo y el vivo al bollo
english_translation: The dead to the grave and the living to the bun
Cultural_Context: Life goes on — focus on the living after loss or tragedy.

source_text: A falta de pan buenas son tortas
english_translation: When there's no bread, cakes are good
Cultural_Context: Be content with what is available when the ideal is not possible.

source_text: El que a buen árbol se arrima buena sombra le cobija
english_translation: He who leans on a good tree gets good shade
Cultural_Context: Associating with good people brings protection and benefits.

source_text: Al mal tiempo buena cara
english_translation: To bad times a good face
Cultural_Context: Show strength and optimism even when facing difficulties.

source_text: Ojos que no ven corazón que no siente
english_translation: Eyes that don't see heart that doesn't feel
Cultural_Context: Ignorance of painful facts spares emotional suffering.

source_text: A río revuelto ganancia de pescadores
english_translation: In troubled river profit for fishermen
Cultural_Context: Chaos and confusion allow clever people to take advantage.

source_text: Camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente
english_translation: The sleeping shrimp is carried by the current
Cultural_Context: Complacency causes you to miss opportunities and fall behind.

source_text: Quien siembra vientos recoge tempestades
english_translation: He who sows winds reaps storms
Cultural_Context: Harmful or negative actions return amplified as consequences.

source_text: El que calla otorga
english_translation: He who is silent grants
Cultural_Context: Not speaking up is often interpreted as agreement or consent.

source_text: El que espera desespera
english_translation: He who waits despairs
Cultural_Context: Passive waiting leads to frustration — act decisively when possible.

source_text: A buen entendedor pocas palabras bastan
english_translation: To a good listener few words suffice
Cultural_Context: Intelligent people understand quickly with minimal explanation.

source_text: A palabras necias oídos sordos
english_translation: To foolish words deaf ears
Cultural_Context: The best response to nonsense is to ignore it completely.

source_text: A cada cerdo le llega su San Martín
english_translation: To every pig comes its Saint Martin's day
Cultural_Context: Everyone eventually faces the consequences of their actions (judgment day arrives).

source_text: El que come y canta por algo se levanta
english_translation: He who eats and sings gets up for something
Cultural_Context: People who enjoy life and stay positive tend to have motivation and energy.

source_text: No hay peor sordo que el que no quiere oír
english_translation: There is no worse deaf person than the one who does not want to hear
Cultural_Context: Willful refusal to listen or accept advice is the most stubborn form of ignorance.

source_text: El que da primero da dos veces
english_translation: He who gives first gives twice
Cultural_Context: Being the first to offer help or generosity creates double the benefit or goodwill.

source_text: El que ríe último ríe mejor
english_translation: He who laughs last laughs best
Cultural_Context: The final outcome determines true success — don't celebrate too early.

source_text: En tierra de ciegos el tuerto es rey
english_translation: In the land of the blind the one-eyed man is king
Cultural_Context: In a group lacking skill or knowledge, even mediocre ability stands out as exceptional.
